newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on late technical selling.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on late technical selling.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower as late technical selling entered the market, traders said.

"There was a lot of technical-type selling late once we made new contract lows," a KCBT trader said. "You also saw profit taking of the December/March spread, which (narrowed) for the first time in days."
KCBT December wheat ended 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower to one cent higher, with Dec down 6-1/2 cents at $4.21-1/4.
New contract lows were set in all KCBT wheat contracts out to July 1997, with Dec hitting a new low at $4.19.
U.S. wheat markets were undermined early as it became clear that Egypt's most recent purchase of U.S. wheat did not include any soft red winter wheat.
"I think the lack of U.S. soft red winter business in that Egyptian purchase is weighing on Chicago and that's taking everything lower," a KCBT trader said at the midsession.
Traders said the Dec/March inverse narrowed to 24 cents Monday after trading as high as 27 cents Friday.

General Mills set the tone early when it sold one million Dec bushels, traders said. E.D. & F. Man International sold three million Dec, much of it late. LFG bear-spread 800,000 March/Dec bushels at 24 to 26 cents. LFG also bought 1.3 million Dec. CIS sold 1.4 million Dec and 900,000 March.
